**Orglet 0.2.4** for Windows.

This is the first build that updates itself. Install it by hand from this page once. From then on, Orglet checks for new versions in the background and switches to them the next time you start it. You can turn that off in Settings → About.

### Workers remember you

Tell an orglet how you like things done and it keeps that for your next chats. Each orglet's settings have a Memory tab where you can read what it kept, edit a line, pin it or delete it. Every answer says how many memories it used. If a worker picks something up right after reading a web page or a file, that memory waits for your review instead of going live.

### Workers can set up the app for you

Ask an orglet for a new crew and it can propose the orglets, the crew, skills, schedules or settings as cards in the chat. One click applies a card, and an orglet can be allowed to apply its own. Every change a worker makes to the app also shows up in Notifications.

When you correct an orglet for the same thing twice, it proposes one sentence to add to its own instructions and shows the chats that led to it. That one always waits for you.

### See what a worker changed

When a worker edits files in its working copy, the answer shows how many files changed and how many lines. Click it to read the diff file by file.

### The sidebar

- Ctrl-click or Shift-click to select several orglets or crews, or use the pencil next to **+**. Archive or delete them together.
- Pick two or more orglets and start a group chat with them.
- Right-click any orglet or crew for its menu.
- The mouse back and forward buttons move between the panels you opened.

### A calmer window

- While a worker runs, one small island sits on the composer and says who is working.
- The bell shows a dot for unread notices, marks what is new, and folds repeats.
- Orglet ships its own fonts. You can pick others in Settings → Appearance.
- Switching between chats no longer flashes a blank pane.
- Settings → Data deletes what the app has kept. Settings → About has the links and this changelog.
- Menus open right next to their button, and OpenCode Zen and Go show OpenCode's logo.

### Runs that finish

- Web research gets past a blocked search and long pages instead of failing.
- Coding runs get more steps, and hand in what they have when they near the limit.
- You can set a chat's permissions and working folder before the first message.
- Claude Code, Codex and Cursor Agent can each run as the account you choose.
- A worker whose command can't reach a local server it started is told why, and tests the app in-process instead.

### Before you install

The installer is still not signed. Windows may say it protected your PC. If you downloaded Setup from this page, choose **More info → Run anyway**.

0.2.3 and earlier don't update themselves, so this one has to be installed by hand. Only a Setup install updates itself. The ZIP doesn't.

Orglet is open source under AGPL-3.0. This release ships for Windows only. Release checklist: [windows-release-gates.md](https://github.com/codepawl/orglet/blob/main/docs/windows-release-gates.md).
